cards.front: After a DNS change, `dig` shows the new IP, but your long-running Python service still sends requests to the old server. Why?
cards.back: It reuses open TCP connections, for example from a connection pool or keep-alive, that were made to the old IP.

cards.front: Postgres on `db-host` listens only on `127.0.0.1:5432`. Reach it from your laptop without opening any new port on the server.
cards.back: `ssh -L 5432:localhost:5432 user@db-host`, then connect to `localhost:5432` on your laptop.

cards.front: You change an A record's IP and lower its TTL from 86400 to 60 in the same edit. Some clients keep using the old IP for hours. Why?
cards.back: Resolvers had cached the old record with the old 86400-second TTL. Lower the TTL first, wait out the old TTL, then change the IP.

cards.front: Your AWS security group allows port 8080 from `192.168.1.20/32`, your laptop's IP at home. Your laptop still times out. Why?
cards.back: Allow your home's public IP instead. The server never sees `192.168.1.20`.

cards.front: Inside a container, the app listens on `127.0.0.1:8000`. You ran `docker run -p 8000:8000`, yet `curl localhost:8000` on the host fails. Why?
cards.back: Bind the app to `0.0.0.0` inside the container.

cards.front: `dig example.com` returns the new IP, but `getent hosts example.com` on the same machine returns the old one. What is the usual cause?
cards.back: An old entry for example.com in `/etc/hosts`.

cards.front: A subnet's network ACL allows inbound TCP 8080 and outbound TCP 8080 only. Clients connecting to port 8080 time out. Why?
cards.back: Replies go to the client's random high source port, which the outbound rule blocks. Allow outbound traffic to ports 1024-65535.

cards.front: You looked up api.example.com before you created its record, and got NXDOMAIN. Now the record exists, but lookups still fail for a while. Why?
cards.back: Resolvers cached the NXDOMAIN answer. They keep returning it until the negative-cache TTL from the zone's SOA record expires.

cards.front: You moved a record to a new server and waited longer than the old TTL. Is it now safe to shut down the old server?
cards.back: Not yet. First check its logs or traffic and wait until requests actually stop.
